source.document: Sourav et al., Discover Artificial Intelligence 6:1403 (2026), doi:10.1007/s44163-026-02355-0

D1.name: BAF - Bank Account Fraud (Base variant)
D1.split: train m=0-5; test m=6-7; validation = last 10% of train, chronological

D3.name: IEEE-CIS Fraud Detection (Vesta)
D3.input_features: 394 transaction columns + 41 identity columns joined on TransactionID
D3.split: TransactionDT < 0.8-quantile train; >= 0.8 test; 5-fold time-series CV with expanding window

D4.name: Elliptic++ transaction graph
D4.split: strict-inductive train t=1-34; test t=35-49; pre/post-shock evaluation

D5.name: DGraph-Fin (Finvolution)
D5.input_features: 17 node features + 11 edge types + edge timestamps
D5.split: temporal node-arrival split; background nodes retained only for message passing

qualifiers: Fraud rate is the dataset-level rate stated by the paper; the evaluated partition's own prevalence is a separate quantity.
